title: Decoherence
seal: Why the cat is not blurred
reading: From 1970, beginning with Dieter Zeh at Heidelberg and developed from 1981 by Wojciech Zurek, physicists study what happens when a quantum system interacts with its surroundings — air molecules, radiation, the apparatus itself. The interaction entangles the system with the environment, and the interference between macroscopically different alternatives becomes unobservable in practice, extraordinarily quickly for large objects. In 1996 Serge Haroche and colleagues in Paris watch this process happen, step by step, to a field of a few light quanta in a cavity. Decoherence explains why we never see interference between a live and a dead cat. It does not, by itself, explain why one outcome occurs rather than another.
detail: Formally, the reduced density matrix of the system becomes diagonal in a 'pointer basis' selected by the interaction. Whether this solves the measurement problem is disputed: many-worlds proponents say it completes the story; others say an additional postulate is still needed to get single outcomes.

claim.label: A continuous process at last
claim.summary: Inference from Schrödinger's preference for continuous processes. His 1952 Dublin remarks suggest sympathy for no-collapse views.
voice: So the appearance of a jump comes from a continuous process, following my equation, when the system meets its surroundings. That is what I hoped. But you say it does not tell us which result occurs — so something is still missing, or something is still being hidden.
claim.reasoning: Continuity restored for the appearance of classicality.

claim.label: The irreversible registration explained
claim.summary: Inference: decoherence gives a dynamical account of the irreversibility Bohr attributed to the classical apparatus.
voice: I have said the apparatus must be described classically, and that registration is irreversible. Here is an account of why that is a good description. I do not think it changes the logical point — we still speak of the result in classical terms.
claim.reasoning: Supports, without replacing, the classical description of apparatus.

claim.label: Explains the look, not the fact
claim.summary: Inference from Einstein's demand for a description of the individual system.
voice: It explains why we do not see interference between the exploded and unexploded keg. It does not tell me whether the keg exploded. That was my question.
claim.reasoning: Appearance of classicality is not a description of the single outcome.

claim.label: Where the cut goes
voice: It tells us where we may safely place the division between the observed system and the means of observation — anywhere after the environment has done its work. That is useful. It does not change what the wave is.

claim.label: No grounds to infer
claim.summary: Speculative. We have no evidence on which to infer Dirac's view; the voice says only what his documented general-discussion remark implies.
voice: I said nature makes a choice. If this process shows how the alternatives stop interfering, it shows when the choice becomes irreversible. It does not show the choice itself.
